formattedAddress: No. 4號, Lane 8, Chifeng St, Guangneng Village, Datong District, Taipei City, Taiwan 103

text.text:
First time here, accept walk-in only and you will need to scan their QR code when you reached.
Food ordered:
Truffle Mushroom Spaghetti - The smell of truffle , taste wise was average ok. I have taste better ones

Service - Good and attentive. No doubt.

text.text: 🌟8/10🌟 The environment is welcoming and the staff are friendly. We visited at tea time and luckily we got direct to sit immediately. The dishes presented very decent and nice, the taste is good but not as good as it look like. My personal favourite will be the pancake, the taste of the cream is rich and creamy. Every corner and the vibes are amazing decorated for pictures. (ˊᵒ̴̶̷̤ ꇴ ᵒ̴̶̷̤ˋ)

text.text:
Ordered the Sicily coffee and a garlic oyster pasta.

The Sicily coffee was surprising as it was refreshing. I had some sweet lemon juice in the coffee. This went well with my window seat as it was very therapeutic.

Can't say the same for the garlic oyster pasta. It was lacking strong garlic flavours for an aglio olio. For the oysters, there were quite a few so the portions are decent.

However, I kept biting into "sand" or the black dirt that exists in shellfish. That ruined my experience.

Visited on a Sunday night at around 630; 15 groups ahead of me but I got my table by 715.

Will recommend the Neapolitan pasta! Did not get to try their pancakes because it was OOS.

Cute little space

text.text: I'm so glad I came back to Waku Waku after failing to get a table on a very busy Saturday with a very long wait. We were able to walk in and be seated immediately for lunch at 2pm. Ordering via QR code was very easy (thx to Google Translate) and our food was brought out very quickly. For our mains we had the fried chicken pasta and the salmon mentaiko pasta. Both dishes were generously portioned with perfectly cooked al dente pasta, and we found ourselves scraping up every bit of sauce off of the plates. Aside from pasta, I REALLY enjoyed the fresh baked bread (crusty yet chewy, with a  fire mentaiko spread) and the chicken wings (roasted instead of fried, fall off the bone, lightly sauced and topped with pine nuts). A couple of delicious refreshing summer drinks completed our meal: an iced Sicilian coffee and an iced daffodil tea. Looking forward to trying their other locations!
